task.description:
ISS-0768 is a BLOCKER, root cause already established by ORCH's own direct source read (see docs/issues/ISS-0768.yaml in full -- no ISSUE-FIXER dispatch needed): lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex never threads opts :: [prefix: String.t()] through any of its Repo calls, so it always queries the default public schema instead of the caller's tenant schema, and POST/GET /roles 500 for every tenant on every deployment. Produce a design artefact enumerating the exact fix -- interfaces and call sites only, no implementation code. This module has ZERO prefix: usage today, unlike lib/letflow/identity.ex's established opts :: [prefix: String.t()] convention (see that module's moduledoc, and lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex for a correct existing usage pattern) -- so do not assume a partial migration; enumerate every affected site from scratch. Cover: (1) role_registry.ex has three public functions that touch Repo -- list_roles/0, upsert_role/2, resolve_role_in_tx/1 -- and two private helpers they delegate to (do_upsert_role/2, insert_or_update_role/2); design the new @spec for each public function taking opts :: [prefix: String.t()] (no default, matching identity.ex's convention), and state exactly which Repo call in each function/helper (Repo.all, Repo.get_by, Repo.get, Repo.transaction, Repo.insert) gets prefix: opts[:prefix] added and how the opts thread through the private helpers and the Repo.transaction closure. (2) routers/identity.ex's handle_list_roles/1 and handle_upsert_role/1 currently call RoleRegistry.list_roles() and RoleRegistry.upsert_role(name, group_id) with no opts at all -- design the call-site change to pass conn.assigns.scoped_opts (or scoped_prefix derived the same way every other route in this module already does -- see handle_create/2, handle_list/2 etc for the established pattern) through to both functions, and update handle_list_roles/handle_upsert_role's own signatures to accept conn (they currently only take conn already, verify by reading, but do not pass opts at all internally) -- read the file yourself for the exact current call shape rather than trusting this description's paraphrase. (3) resolve_role_in_tx/1's own moduledoc says it is called from inside a caller's own Repo.transaction (a future S3 applyTransition) with no repo/connection argument -- decide and state explicitly whether this function also needs an opts param for this fix's scope (no current caller exists in the codebase today per a grep, but the moduledoc implies a future one) and give REVIEWER-checkable reasoning either way. (4) State what git blame/log investigation ELIXIR-DEV must run to answer ISS-0768's 'regression vs always-broken' acceptance criterion (e.g. git log -p --follow -- lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex, checking whether any prior version ever threaded opts) -- do not answer the regression question yourself, just specify the exact commands and what evidence would decide it, since ELIXIR-DEV is the implementer who must record the finding. Write the design artefact to lib/letflow/design/ following this project's existing naming convention (see lib/letflow/design/req073-identity-user-routes.md and req074-identity-group-routes.md for the two nearest siblings in the same router module). Branch feature/WF03-ISS0768-20260921 is already checked out in this worktree (c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\letflow-wf03-iss0768) -- work there. Hard rule, no exceptions: never push directly to main -- every change lands via branch -> PR -> CI green -> merge, pre-authorized under humanless operation per docs/migration/decisions/0004-humanless-pipeline.md, but the branch/PR/merge discipline itself is never skippable. Commit your design doc and this handoff file (status flipped to COMPLETED) to the current branch when done; do not push to main directly.

REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILed this design (see handoffs/WF03-ISS0768-20260921/step-02-code-design-validator.json, committed c73793e1) for containing literal implementation code, not signatures-only. Specifically: (a) lines 48-50, the exact rewritten call Repo.all(from(t in TenantRole, order_by: [asc: t.name]), prefix: opts[:prefix]); (b) lines 118-125, the exact rewritten Repo.insert(conflict_target: :name, on_conflict: [set: [group_id: group_id]], returning: true, prefix: opts[:prefix]); (c) lines 141-143, 148-150, 159-161, 165-167, literal router handler-body rewrites (handle_list_roles(conn, conn.assigns.scoped_opts), defp handle_list_roles(conn, opts), etc). Fix by editing the existing lib/letflow/design/iss0768-role-registry-tenant-prefix.md file in place (do not create a second design doc): strip every fenced code block in section 1.1, 1.4, and all of section 2 that shows a full rewritten call or function head, and replace each with PROSE describing exactly which argument/keyword-list option is added or changed at that call site (name the function, the call, and the new argument in a sentence -- do not show the resulting code). Keep the @spec / def name/arity signature-only blocks exactly as they are (e.g. lines 33-36, 56-63, 73-80, 105-112) -- CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR confirmed those are correctly signature-only and is not asking you to touch them. Everything else in the design (the Repo-call inventory, the router call-site targets, the resolve_role_in_tx/1 out-of-scope reasoning, the section-4 regression-investigation commands) was independently verified correct against the real source and must not be changed in substance -- this rework is a presentation-only fix (code blocks -> prose), not a redesign. This is the same handoff you already completed once (status was COMPLETED with a PASS self-report); flip it to COMPLETED again when this rework is done, following HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's normal completion procedure -- there is no separate IN_PROGRESS claim step required beyond what you'd do for any handoff already in your hands.
